subject: missing window argument for traceplot() in RStan?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: missing window argument for traceplot() in RStan?
parts:
I'm trying to run one of my old knitr documents and I'm
getting an error executing a traceplot

traceplot(fit,
c("Omega", "alpha", "beta", "sigma_uv", "rho_uv",
"uv[1,1]", "uv[1,2]", "uv[30,1]", "uv[30,2]",
"lp__"),
inc_warmup=FALSE,
window=c(3001,3200));

that says

Quitting from lines 398-404 (dorazio-et-al-knitr.Rmd)
Error: Unknown parameters: window

I don't see "window" in the doc any more. Was this an intentional
break in backward compatiblity? If so, how should I be doing this now?

- Bob

              "lp__"),
            inc_warmup=FALSE,
            window=c(3001,3200));

that says

  Quitting from lines 398-404 (dorazio-et-al-knitr.Rmd)
  Error: Unknown parameters: window

I don't see "window" in the doc any more.  Was this an intentional
break in backward compatiblity?  If so, how should I be doing this now?

The window argument seems to have disappeared in

cb90cd423efec70d4a3d431765c9a70a54712cdb

when we went to ggplot2 plots. Jonah does the windowing thing in ShinyStan, so I guess he would know how to do it in a static ggplot2 plot.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: missing window argument for traceplot() in RStan?
parts:
There was a break in backwards compatibility with the plots when we switched to ggplot2. The x-axis is just iteration number so 
you can do 

traceplot(fit) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(a, b))

to get the window between iterations a and b. I believe I put an example of this in the documentation for the traceplot method, which you can pull up with ?rstan::traceplot or help("traceplot", "rstan").

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: missing window argument for traceplot() in RStan?
parts: If you prefer we can add the window argument back in. The old traceplot method (using base R graphics) needed that argument because it wasn't possible to change the window after creating the plot. Since it's so easy to do with ggplot2 I kind of like not having the argument.

Thanks.

I read the doc and the examples and didn't even notice
that example was relevant to what I was looking for. I was
searching for "window" and "thin", both in the doc and online.

Is there a reason you decided to break backward compatibility?
It's very very hard on naive R users like me, who can easily waste hours
when things go off the rails and then lose confidence in a package's
stability. (I spent half an hour searching, then sent out the first mail,
then gave up and just changed the tutorial, then got Jonah's email,
then reverted my changes and updated, then sent out this email.)

One approach is to deprecate old behavior and give users
warnings on how to fix things right in the program itself.

- Bob
